_comment: Runtime configuration for the agent system. Contains NO secrets: a
provider's credential is named here by the GitHub Actions secret that
holds it, never by value. Changing a model or a retry limit must not
require touching workflow logic - that is the whole point of this file.
3. agentlib defaults            - per codebase (hard caps live here and

anthropic._api_note: api_key_env, endpoint and api_version are for the direct Messages API calls the cheap automations make (automations below), stdlib urllib, no SDK. The roles above go through the claude CLI instead.

jev._note: TypeSafe's System One typed-decision model, asked narrow questions in shadow by the cheap automations (wiki/GeneralContext/Architecture/work-modes.md). Called only through .ai/bin/ask_jev.py, never via invoke_agent.sh: it answers typed questions, it does not run as an agent.

manager._why: Strategy, ambiguous-failure interpretation, escalation calls. Invoked rarely and only when reasoning is actually needed.

test_agent._why: Turning stated acceptance criteria into tests is bounded work against a contract the Director already wrote.

code_agent._why: Bounded implementation against committed tests. Escalates rather than re-deciding architecture.

distiller._why: Adds prose interpretation on top of an already-parsed failure structure. Cheapest tier; optional (see features.distiller_model_pass).

context_maintainer._why: Small targeted wiki edits against a known diff.

automations._note: The cheap automations of wiki/GeneralContext/Architecture/work-modes.md: one narrow model call each, from main's copy in a workflow, priced from the response's usage against telemetry.prices. Caps here can only lower agentlib's own (cisummary.MAX_TOKENS, MAX_LOG_CHARS; coverage.MAX_TOKENS, MAX_TEST_CHARS; drift.MAX_TOKENS, MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS; wikiprop.MAX_TOKENS, MAX_DIFF_CHARS; directorreview.MAX_TOKENS, MAX_DIFF_CHARS).

ci_summary._why: Prompts/04 automation 1: one sentence naming the likely cause of a red agent/* PR run, beside ciresult's deterministic parse. .ai/bin/ci_summary.py, run by .github/workflows/ci-summary.yml.

coverage._why: Prompts/04 automation 2: which acceptance criteria no test pins, from the spec on main and the test files an agent/* PR changes; advisory, fails nothing. jev was asked .ai/questions/coverage.json in shadow until 2026-10-16; ask_jev switches it. .ai/bin/coverage_check.py, run by .github/workflows/coverage-check.yml.

spec_drift._why: Prompts/04 automation 3: which paths, links and names a task spec uses that the code on main does not have, dispatched by hand before a unit. Paths and links are checked without a model; Haiku is asked only for names in the prose, each re-checked against the code. jev was asked .ai/questions/drift.json in shadow until 2026-10-16; ask_jev switches it. .ai/bin/spec_drift.py, run by .github/workflows/spec-drift.yml.

wiki_proposal._why: Prompts/04 automation 4: when an agent/* PR merges, whether the merged diff changed something the wiki/CodeContext/Modules/ files its spec names document; the answer is a comment on the merged PR holding a patch the human applies by hand (option (a), decided 2026-10-13). Nothing is committed. .ai/bin/wiki_proposal.py, run by .github/workflows/wiki-proposal.yml.

director_review._why: Prompts/09 deliverable 5: a Director PR is reviewed by the one human who directed it and merges through the admin bypass, so an independent model reads every non-agent/*, non-bot PR of this repository touching .ai/ or .github/ against philosophy.md and threat-model.md on main, and lists safety regressions by enforcement grade; advisory, fails nothing. Sonnet 5.5, not Haiku: the human, 2026-10-19 (human-decisions.md section 8), Haiku is too light for workflow diffs. About $0.05 a PR. .ai/bin/director_review.py, run by .github/workflows/director-review.yml.

_prices_note: USD per million tokens, the provider's list prices as of 2026-10-09.
Used only for the FALLBACK estimate: a record's cost_usd is the provider's
own figure for the call (the CLI envelope's total_cost_usd) whenever the
provider gave one, with cost_source 'provider' (handoff.md section 10, D6).
Cache rates are the provider's documented multiples of the input price:
cache read 0.1x, 5-minute cache write 1.25x, 1-hour cache write 2x. The read
and 1-hour write rates reproduce the CLI's own total_cost_usd exactly on a
5-minute rate is not exercised by that sample. An unpriced model records a
null estimate rather than a guessed one. claude-haiku-4-5 is listed under
both its dated and undated ids. The *-5-5 rows are for the coming model
switch (handoff.md section 10.3 item 5); no role uses them yet.
Exception: claude-opus-5-5 cache reads are listed at $0.20, i.e. 0.05x, not
0.1x. Its cache writes and claude-haiku-5-5's cache rates are not on the
price list consulted, so those keep the 1.25x/2x/0.1x multiples, unverified.
jev/jev-latest is TypeSafe's list price as of 2026-10-13: $0.042 per million
input tokens, output free. ask_jev.py prices each call from the usage the
response reports, keyed by the model requested (jev-latest), not the release

_auto_merge_note: features.auto_merge is false and the workflows never set it true. Every agent-authored branch reaches main through a human-approved PR.
